Amendments made after a number was computed are listed in `amendments`; there are none.

hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3, an arm on the candidate (s3c). Development tier
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)
why: (s3c)'s two settlement terms, `settlement_coupon` and `settlement_bill`, are scheduled fields of the target row (spread_mr_calendar.TERMS, scheduled = True, span (0,)). metadata/sources.json declares a settlement public at 15:00 on the panel day before it settles, so `readable_offsets` keeps the terms at lead 1 only. The announcement dating is built and measured (#541; metadata/settlement_announcement_dating.json, repo_model.settlement_dating) but not in force. The arms read it as a measurement.

candidates.definition: (s3c) with its two settlement flags available at leads 2 to 5 when the auction was announced by the decision instant: for the forecast made at lead h on decision day D, the flag of the coupon (bill) term of target day T = D + h panel days is 1 when the offering amounts of the coupon (bill) auctions settling on T that had been announced by 16:00 on D sum to more than zero. Everything else is (s3)'s: the other terms, the Huber fit (k = 1.345), the ridge of 5, the pool of standardised residuals and the direct pairs; the SRF cap at the line from full allotment, margin 0 bp, is applied to its quantiles exactly as to (s3)'s (repo_model.s3c_candidate, unchanged). At lead 1 the arm is (s3c) cell for cell (the study checks it and refuses to write a record otherwise)

dating.declaration: metadata/settlement_announcement_dating.json (#541, Eleonora, 10 October 2026), read with repo_model.settlement_dating.load_result_dating and auction_results, unchanged: an auction's settlement date and offering amount are public from 12:00 America/New_York on its announcemt_date
dating.source: the Fiscal Data auctions snapshot the published panel builds its gross settlement columns from (tests/fixtures/snapshots/funding_inputs/treasury_auctions/), the same records as repo_model.net_settlement reads (metadata/net_settlement.json also stamps the announcement at 12:00)
dating.instant: 16:00 America/New_York on the decision day, the published records' decision time. An announcement stamped 12:00 on or before the decision day is public at it; any decision instant from 12:00 to 23:59 gives the same sums, so the result does not depend on the 16:00 choice
dating.bill_caveat: Lens E's caveat (docs/reviews/2026-10-19-five-lens/lens-E-data-plumbing.md, item G, and the dating file's own evidence): Treasury publishes no clock time for an announcement, and the 12:00 instant for a cash management bill is unverified. A cash management bill is ad hoc, announced the same or the previous day, sometimes auctioned at 11:30 and settled at T+0 or T+1; if one is announced after 12:00 on the decision day the arm counts it too early. The bill leg is therefore read with that caveat, said on the page and not removed; the share of bill settlement days that carry a cash management bill is reported, and the bill leg is also reported without them (the days on which a cash management bill settles are a group of their own)
dating.lead_1: at lead 1 the arms read the panel's flags and #1273's net exactly as (s3c) and (s3c-net) do; the study compares the announced gross with the panel's gross columns on every scored target day and reports the days that differ (the dating declaration states they agree at h = 1)
dating.new_read_path: repo_model.s3c_announced.AnnouncedTermTable and AnnouncedNetSizeTable are new read paths; tests/test_s3c_announced.py holds their leakage test with one recorded mutation (the instant of the figure taken from the target day instead of the decision day; LookAheadError), and the test that the published asof rule and the live record's features still refuse a settlement column beyond lead 1
dating.training: a training pair reads the figure of its own decision, the target row less the lead, so a training figure and a forecast figure are the same function of the same announcements

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.pressure_probability: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp), the probability read off the 23 quantiles as 1 - F(floor(tau) + 0.5), F linear between them (spread_mean_reversion.exceedance), the event strict and on whole basis points (data.exceeds_bp)
primary.calibration: the coverage of the central 90% band (q5 to q95, closed) of every model, beside (s3c)'s, pooled and by regime; a rate, reported as a mean and not tested
primary.comparisons: both arms paired with (s3c), (s3) and (s3c-net), and against B1, B1' and B2; (s3c-ann-net) also against (s3c-ann); each leg reference against (s3c) and the arm it belongs to

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1288, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed (most of a group's days score alike) the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): an arm is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.splits: pooled; by lead (the gain should sit at h = 2 to 5); by regime (the declared regimes); by pressure-day type of the target day (turn_days.reporting_day_type, the record in force); by calendar target-day type (#1115's groups); by target month (2026 window); by the settlement-day type of the target at each lead h = 1..5 (a coupon settlement day, a bill settlement day, a day with neither: the panel's gross settlement above zero on the target day); and, at each lead, by whether the changed term is non-zero at the decision (an announced coupon or bill settlement, or a non-zero announced net, on the target day) against the other decision days. The intervals of a group of target days keep the current method (the group's days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions and #1228 will decide
scoring.references_by_split: every split is tested against every reference of the arm (the benchmarks included) except the two announced-term splits, which are tested against (s3c), (s3c-net) and, for (s3c-ann-net), (s3c-ann) only; a leg reference is tested against (s3c) alone, on every split but the announced-term ones
scoring.identical_groups: a group in which an arm's score equals the reference's on every day is listed as identical and not tested against it; a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested

effect.what: the fitted effect of each changed term in bp: for (s3c-ann), bp per flagged settlement day (the standardised effect of the refit the forecast used times the scale at the anchor in bp, spread_mr_state_calendar.StateEstimate.effect), for (s3c-ann-net) bp per USD 100 bn of net settlement (repo_model.s3c_net.bp_per_100bn), at each lead 1..5
effect.report: by lead and by regime of the target day: the mean over the scored decision days, with the 90% stationary-bootstrap interval of that mean over decision days (an interval over days that share refits, not a sampling interval for the coefficient), the share of days on which the term was in the fit

reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c) stays the candidate until she rules on the result.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the lead, regime and settlement-day-type splits beside it.
The announced terms act at leads 2 to 5; the lead-1 cells are (s3c)'s and (s3c-net)'s by construction, so the average over h = 1..5 is read beside the leads 2 to 5 rows.
The bill leg is read with Lens E's caveat on the announcement time of a cash management bill.
The page ends with marked questions for Eleonora with numbered options and defaults that change no claim.
